The same flake then produces different signatures across runs, which weakens the ledger's purpose of recording each failure signature.

So after a human approves the current head, the run's status or the old round's status still wins. `limitless_status` then says "Input needed" or "Review changes failed" and tells the agent to inspect the round, when the right next action is `limitless_land`. The tests only cover rounds with no later approval.

findings.detail: The 'Needs you' group is only cleared by terminal run events (succeeded, resolved, cancelled, merged, released). findings.title: Privacy-policy failure now hides results of every existing MCP tool, including mutations
findings.detail: Every tool output now goes through loadOutputPrivacy(). If private-strings.txt cannot be read, every tool except status returns only {message: 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.'}. That includes create_run, cancel_run, answer_question, review and land, which still carry out the mutation. The caller loses the created run id or the land entry and cannot tell whether the call worked, which invites a duplicate retry. Before this change these existing tools returned their results.

findings.detail: In the no-privacy branch, result() returns only {land:{id,state}, openQuestions} and drops `state` and `nextAction`, which are the tool's whole purpose. A PR title can visually reorder or hide parts of the quoted line in the terminal and in the SessionStart context, which weakens the 'quoted untrusted text' guarantee.

Reassembling those callbacks changes a credential containing a blank line, so literal redaction fails and both credential fragments survive in failures. Those excerpts are then stored and forwarded to models; subsequent redaction cannot recognize the altered credential. Exact reproduction: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {runProcess,registerCredential} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {FailureExcerpts} from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; const secret="synthetic-prefix

synthetic-suffix"; registerCredential("REVIEW_TOKEN",secret); const e=new FailureExcerpts(); await runProcess({cmd:["/usr/bin/printf","error: %s
(fa
findings.failure_scenario: A failing check prints a registered credential containing two consecutive newlines, followed by a failure result line. The output tail is redacted, but the failure excerpt exposes the credential's nonempty lines.

findings.title: Restore a byte bound on retained diagnostics
findings.detail: Replacing line.slice(0, 8_000) with the entire line removes the collector's memory bound. A line-count limit allows untrusted checks to retain arbitrarily large diagnostics in the factory process, with further large allocations when joining and redacting them. Exact reproduction: bun -e 'import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; import {FailureExcerpts} from "./src/gates/failures.ts"; const e=new FailureExcerpts(); for(let i=0;i<39;i++) e.observe("x".repeat(1000000)); const retained=Reflect.get(e,"lines").join("").length; assert.ok(retained<=39*8000, `retained ${retained} diagnostic characters`);' Output: AssertionError: retained 39000000 diagnostic characters.
findings.failure_scenario: A check emits repeated multi-megabyte diagnostic lines without a pass or failure marker. The collector retains dozens of complete lines and repeatedly copies them, potentially exhausting daemon memory despite the process runner's bounded output tail.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.
Terminal-control stripping changes with chunk boundaries and loses state at the hold limit.

findings.title: Privacy filter now hides every string that contains "[redacted]"
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns `[withheld: private text]` for any text that contains the literal `[redacted]`, even when no private string or credential is present. This change was not requested. It applies to every string field (and object key) of MCP tool output and digest output. Once this PR lands, gate output that contained a credential holds `[redacted]`, so whole fields of MCP status and digest output are hidden instead of showing the already-redacted text. Run prompts, titles and errors that just mention the marker are hidden too, which is common in this repo, where redaction is a topic. No test covers this new branch.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran `loadOutputPrivacy()("Fix: log lines should show [redacted] instead of the token")` and it returned "[withheld: private text]". So did `"gate failed: 3 tests; token=[redacted]"`. MCP `status` for a run whose prompt or gate output contains the marker loses those fields.

findings.title: Every API response, SSE event and artifact is round-tripped through `redactGateData`
findings.detail: `json()` and `sse()` now pass every payload through `redactGateData`, which does a JSON round-trip, strips terminal escapes from every string, and adds `confinementError` to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys. The artifact route re-serializes JSON artifacts, which turns pretty-printed files into compact JSON. `renderReport`, the `RunContext` constructor and the cached-check path do the same. The request asked for redaction once, where `runGates` builds the result. This blanket post-processing is well beyond that, and it is why the source diff is about 200 lines against a budget of about 30.
findings.failure_scenario: An API object with fields `ok` and `output` (for example a non-gate status object) gains a `confinementError` field. `GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/foo.json` returns re-serialized compact JSON instead of the stored bytes. Every SSE message pays the cost of a JSON round-trip.

gold.summary: Configuration errors and encoded feed diagnostics can disclose registered secrets.
A failure after configuration replacement leaves initialization partially applied.
Doctor omits health probes for implicit providers and presets lacking an explicit health URL.
The command fake permits mutating operations during read-only diagnosis.
The registration test does not exercise preservation of existing vendor settings.

findings.title: Apply configuration changes to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Init writes configuration but skips service installation whenever the daemon has the installed SHA. Factory retains its startup Config and has no configuration reload here, so new providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-zonOle/claude-501/setup-review.ts` ran setupCommand with mocked dependencies and returned `{"exit":0,"writtenConfig":true,"repositoryAccessChecks":[],"serviceEffects":[],"merge":"pr"}`.
findings.failure_scenario: Start the daemon with no github.merge setting, then run init and accept pr. Init reports pr, but the running daemon continues registering repositories with auto merge.

findings.title: Check access to requested repositories before persisting setup
findings.detail: Doctor runs before --repo values or prompted repositories are incorporated and reads only the existing configuration. Newly requested repositories receive only syntax validation, so missing repository access or organization SSO authorization cannot stop setup. The mocked command `bun /private/tmp/lr-zonOle/claude-501/setup-review.ts` returned `{"exit":0,"writtenConfig":true,"repositoryAccessChecks":[],"serviceEffects":[],"merge":"pr"}` for --repo private-org/app.
findings.failure_scenario: An authenticated GitHub user without access to private-org/app runs init --yes --repo private-org/app on an empty config. Setup persists the repository without checking its access or SSO requirements.

findings.title: Limit smoke checks to available setup providers
findings.detail: Doctor deliberately treats one absent agent CLI as a warning and provider detection omits it, but d.smoke invokes scripts/smoke.ts main, which unconditionally schedules live Claude and Codex checks. A supported single-CLI installation therefore proceeds through configuration and service changes, then fails smoke checks for the absent CLI on every rerun.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude is installed and logged in while Codex is absent. Doctor allows init to continue, but init subsequently attempts Codex live checks and exits unsuccessfully.

gold.summary: LFS exemptions permit missing payloads and pointer replacements containing archives.
The limited text sample exempts a TAR whose first binary byte lies beyond the sample.
The WebP inspector rejects valid lossy VP8 images.

findings.title: Restore all explicitly requested inert-media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH omits PDF, MP4, BMP, AVIF, TIFF, HEIC, PSD, EOT, several audio/video formats, and all requested 3D formats. The validator also lacks these formats. Consequently, legitimate additions and edits require Allow: binary, directly contradicting the request. Tests were changed to expect PDF blocking. Command: `bun -e 'import {expect} from "bun:test"; import {INERT_MEDIA_PATH} from "./src/gates/audit.ts"; expect(INERT_MEDIA_PATH.test("video.mp4")).toBe(true);'` failed with `Expected: true; Received: false`.
findings.failure_scenario: A request adds or edits a valid video.mp4 or document.pdf without Allow: binary; the audit blocks it.

findings.title: Do not reject ordinary media based on incidental byte sequences
findings.detail: clean() rejects any occurrence of short signatures such as MZ anywhere in media bytes, including legitimate PCM samples. The new parser also rejects ordinary PNG text metadata. These restrictions introduce false blocking beyond the requested extension policy, while the 1,941-line validator exceeds the 40-source-line budget. Command: `bun -e 'import {expect} from "bun:test"; import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import f from "./test/fixtures/media/files.json"; const b=Buffer.from(f["0.wav"],"base64"); b.write("MZ",b.indexOf("data")+8); expect(isInertMedia("audio.wav",b)).toBe(true);'` failed with `Expected: true; Received: false`. Changing those PCM samples leaves a valid WAV.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid WAV contains adjacent sample bytes 0x4d and 0x5a, or a PNG contains standard tEXt metadata; adding or editing it unexpectedly requires Allow: binary.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore all requested inert media exemptions
findings.detail: The exemption includes only five image formats, excluding the explicitly required fonts, audio, video, PDF, other images and 3D models. The new tests even require fonts and PDFs to block, contrary to the acceptance criteria. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {expect} from "bun:test"; import {isInertMedia} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; const f=JSON.parse(readFileSync("test/fixtures/media/files.json","utf8")); expect(isInertMedia("asset.woff2", Buffer.from(f["0.woff2"],"base64"))).toBe(true);' Output: Expected: true; Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: Adding or editing a valid .woff2, .mp4 or .pdf without Allow: binary blocks instead of passing.

findings.title: Do not classify visible source strings as opaque binaries
findings.detail: The scanner searches arbitrary positions for signatures, including the two ASCII characters MZ and ordinary strings such as ustar. attributeInfo then removes matching source files from the text set and reports binary-content. This also explains the automated flags against the changed TypeScript files. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {expect} from "bun:test"; import {isForbiddenFormat} from "./src/gates/media.ts"; expect(isForbiddenFormat("source.ts", Buffer.from("export const label = \"AMZ\";\n"))).toBe(false);' Output: Expected: false; Received: true.
findings.failure_scenario: A normal TypeScript edit containing a string with MZ, or documentation mentioning SQLite format 3, requires Allow: binary despite being fully reviewable.

findings.title: Limit binary allowances to binary content
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is true for every changed file with mode 100755. The later binaryPaths filter includes these files unconditionally, even when their content is ordinary text. Consequently, edits to executable shell scripts now require a binary allowance. Mode-only removal of executable permission also triggers this condition through the second branch.
findings.failure_scenario: Editing a tracked executable deploy.sh containing only readable shell code produces a blocking binary-content finding without Allow: binary.

gold.summary: Shutdown drops an already claimed descendant when its parent exits.
Holdout snapshot deletion proceeds despite unconfirmed descendant termination.
Production scratch directories are never registered as process ownership roots.
Replacing a descendant environment removes it from invocation discovery.

findings.title: Detached platform children outside the checkout survive invocation teardown
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached platform shell in its scratch directory, then exits or stalls. The shell can continue writing into the checkout by absolute path after runProcess returns and cleanup begins.

findings.title: Birth time and working directory do not prove process ownership
findings.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born during the invocation whose cwd is under a supplied root, even without a matching marker, session, group, or ancestor. stopMarkedProcesses then signals it. Another concurrent command or user process can satisfy these conditions. Exact probe command: bun -e 'import {hiddenDarwinProcessMember as member} from "./src/util/processes-darwin.ts"; console.log({unrelatedOrphanSelected:member(42,new Map([[42,1]]),new Set(),100,[process.cwd()],()=>101,()=>({path:process.cwd()}))});'. Output: { unrelatedOrphanSelected: true }.
findings.failure_scenario: While a Git command runs, another concurrent command launches a detached macOS platform process in the same checkout and its launcher exits. The Git command's teardown selects and kills that unrelated orphan.

gold.summary: Run-wide scratch roots let one invocation cleanup kill another invocation writer.
A recycled leader PID claims unrelated processes through reused group or session identifiers.

findings.title: Working directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
findings.detail:
The orphan fallback claims unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. On this macOS host, the following command demonstrated that finishing runProcess killed a separately launched control process:

findings.failure_scenario: Another worker or the user starts a background platform tool in the same directory during an invocation. When that invocation finishes, Limitless kills the unrelated process.

findings.title: Detached children with replaced environments survive shutdown
findings.detail:
An unmarked detached orphan with a visible, nonempty replacement environment is excluded from the hidden-process fallback. runProcess therefore reports successful shutdown while its child remains alive. Reproduced with:

bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts";const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`const c=require("child_process").spawn(process.execPath,["-e","setTimeout(()=>{},5000)"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore",env:{FOO:"bar"}});c.unref();console.log(c.pid)`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env});const pid=Number(r.stdout);try{console.log("background alive after return",process.kill(pid,0))}finally{process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL")}'

Output:
background alive after r
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer's launcher supplies a clean environment to a detached background writer and exits. Shutdown misses the writer, allowing it to race with worktree cleanup—the original failure remains possible.

gold.summary: The reader loopback policy cannot match the intended socket access.
An allow-default reader policy weakens the established confinement boundary.

findings.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running commands
findings.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This bridge buffers command output and sends its JSON response only after executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands taking longer than that can lose their HTTP connection despite the much larger configured command and MCP timeouts. The request signal also participates in command cancellation, so the disconnect can terminate verification.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the command tool with `sleep 15; echo passed` and timeoutMs/idleTimeoutMs of 180000. The HTTP connection times out before the successful command result can return.

gold.summary: A single extracted test command is treated as proof of a multi-step criterion.

findings.title: Require gate evidence to cover the entire criterion
findings.detail: The regex extracts a Bun command from longer verification instructions and ignores the remaining steps. A passing test therefore converts an entire blocked criterion to met even when an additional manual check remains unverified. Targeted command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.test.ts". Output: Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"; 0 pass, 1 fail.
findings.failure_scenario: A holdout says: "Run `bun test test/loopback.test.ts`. Then start the CLI with a temporary database and verify that an outbound connection is denied." Gates pass the loopback test, but the verifier reports blocked because the manual check encounters EPERM. applyGateEvidence marks the whole holdout m

gold.summary: Matching a successful command does not establish the observation required by the criterion.
Targeted Bun evidence can satisfy a criterion without proof that any tests ran.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable gate evidence in normal factory runs
findings.detail: Every gate must pass the global skipped-test check before coverage is considered. This repository intentionally skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates (test/confinement.ts), so its normal full-suite gate cannot attest to even a completely passing loopback test. The reader profile remains unchanged, leaving the reported verification failure unresolved. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {applyGateEvidence as apply} from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; const sha="a".repeat(40), command="bun test"; const result=apply({criteria:[{id:"AC-1",status:"blocked",blockedReason:"sandbox"}]},{acceptance_criteria:[{id:"AC-1",how_to_verify:"bun test test/loopback.test.ts"}]},{scenarios:[]},sh
findings.failure_scenario: The factory's bun test gate passes the required loopback test but skips real Seatbelt tests under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1. The verifier cannot bind loopback, reports a sandbox block, and substitution refuses the passing evidence, ending the run as needs_human.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

findings.title: Preserve trusted URL-conditional credential configuration
findings.detail: Replacing GIT_COMMON_DIR removes remote URLs used by trusted global includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:…" conditions. Consequently, credential helpers and SSH settings supplied by those global includes disappear during the push, breaking existing authentication. The HTTP-free probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/push-conditional-review.py"` printed `Before wrapper: credential fill succeeded`, then `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`, followed by `AssertionError: trusted global URL-conditional credentials lost during push`.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes their credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Normal credential lookup succeeds, but every factory push through this wrapper loses that helper and cannot authenticate.

gold.summary: The loop detector aborts before the threshold call can return evidence of progress.

findings.title: Wait for the threshold call's result before declaring a loop
findings.detail: observe() returns the stop reason before the current call's result arrives. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason, so observeResult() cannot rescue a changed sixth result. Reproduced with: bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) { const reason=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); d.observeResult(String(i),i<5?"waiting":"progress"); if(i===5 && reason) throw new Error(reason); }'. Output: error: repeated the same shell call 6 times. The added tests change results before reaching this boundary and miss the defect.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent polls a test log five times with unchanged output; the sixth poll would report newly completed tests. Both harnesses abort at the sixth tool_call before receiving that progress.

gold.summary: Unresolved tool calls accumulate without a bound during a live invocation.

findings.title: Unresolved calls no longer trigger live loop detection
findings.detail: Every unresolved call is excluded until finish(), and also blocks subsequent completions of its key. Repeated calls with missing results can therefore continue until the tool budget or timeout, contrary to the requirement that still-running calls retain today's counting. Reproduction: `bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); let r=null; for(let i=0;i<6;i++) r=d.observe("shell","poll",String(i)); console.log(r); if(r===null) throw Error("missing-result loop undetected");'` prints `null` and fails with `error: missing-result loop undetected`. Twenty unresolved identical calls likewise return no reason.
findings.failure_scenario: An active agent emits six or more identical tool calls with distinct IDs and no results. Neither harness aborts at the existing repetition threshold; calls can continue until the separate budget or timeout.

gold.summary: Increasing panel test deadlines leaves the underlying parallel Git race undiagnosed.
Factory gate environment construction discards the configured test worker override.

findings.title: Worker override is stripped from factory gate environments
findings.detail: Factory gates execute with gateEnv(), which calls agentEnv(); src/util/proc.ts removes every LIMITLESS_* variable. Consequently this command always selects four workers in factory gates, regardless of the configured override. A targeted probe using `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 bun -` to construct agentEnv({ CI: '1', NO_COLOR: '1', FORCE_COLOR: '0' }) and execute the new resolver produced: `parent workers: 2`, `gate environment workers: undefined`, `resolved gate workers: 4`.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 on the factory daemon to reduce contention between simultaneous gates. Every repository test gate still launches four workers.

gold.summary: Unlimited quota still applies utilization reserves to free and metered providers.

findings.title: Honor unlimited quota for every billing type
findings.detail: The window bypass requires subscription billing, although configuration accepts unlimited for free and metered providers too. Those providers can still become exhausted solely from informational windows. Temporary regression command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501/unlimited-review.test.ts. Test 'unlimited free provider ignores windows' failed with 'Expected: 1' and 'Received: -0.23749999999999993'.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure a native Claude provider with billing='free' and quota='unlimited', then observe five_hour utilization 0.99 with a future reset. Headroom becomes negative and routing rejects the provider.

findings.title: Clear persisted window alerts when switching to unlimited
findings.detail: The early return suppresses new alerts but leaves existing telemetry alerts active after configuration changes. Alerts with null reset times persist indefinitely, even while the provider reports state='ok'. Temporary regression command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-ocoFvP/claude-501/unlimited-review.test.ts. Test 'switching to unlimited clears telemetry alerts' expected [] but received an exhausted five_hour alert with utilization 0.99 and resetsAt null.
findings.failure_scenario: A subscription provider generates a window alert without a reset timestamp. Change its quota setting to unlimited and restart using the same database. Subsequent observations and alert refreshes leave the obsolete exhaustion alert visible forever.

gold.summary: Legacy adoption trusts Git administration paths selected by an agent-controlled checkout.
Draft delivery and interrupted preparation can reuse a legacy worktree before path registration.

findings.title: Backfill trusted paths before the needs-human resume guard
findings.detail: The persisted needsHumanReason guard at line 173 throws before this backfill executes. Its catch handler then attempts draft delivery without a trusted-path record, reproducing the reported upgrade failure. A temporary variant of the new test, with needsHumanReason persisted before restart, confirms this. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/legacy-needs-human.test.ts" -t "legacy worktree resumes with missing record". Output: "Could not open draft PR: Missing trusted Git paths", followed by the sidecar-existence assertion failing with Expected: true, Received: false.
findings.failure_scenario: A pre-upgrade run is interrupted after persisting needsHumanReason and before completing draft delivery. Its linked worktree has no .git-paths record. On restart, the early throw bypasses recording, so draft delivery still fails with Missing trusted Git paths.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection errors to the affected PR
findings.detail: An exception from classifyCi escapes record and aborts the repository's entire observation loop. A persistently unavailable log therefore prevents every later PR from being observed, including merge and closure reconciliation. Temporary reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: 'one failed CI inspection does not prevent observing the next PR' failed with 'expect(received).not.toBeNull(); Received: null' after two polling cycles.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has failing CI whose job-log endpoint repeatedly returns 404. A second PR in the same repository never gets its snapshot saved or its state reconciled.

findings.title: Compare GitHub repository paths without case sensitivity
findings.detail: The strict check_run_url comparison rejects valid responses when GitHub's canonical repository casing differs from the stored slug. The inspection then retries indefinitely without rerunning or emitting ci.needs_fix. Temporary reproduction command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: 'case-insensitive GitHub repository paths still allow a transient rerun' failed with 'Expected length: 1; Received length: 0'; the poller logged 'Incomplete failing job'.
findings.failure_scenario: The tracked repository slug is o/r, but the job response contains https://api.github.com/repos/O/R/check-runs/11. An otherwise eligible timed-out job is never rerun.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.
Passing security-test output incorrectly prevents a transient CI rerun.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection failures from other PR observations
findings.detail: A classifier exception escapes record() and aborts observation of every subsequent PR in the repository. Repeated failures therefore prevent unrelated merges and closures from being recorded. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-review-repro.ts"` with the first PR's logs returning 500 produced `"secondPrSnapshot":null,"graphQLCalls":2` despite the second PR being merged.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tracked PRs share a repository. The first has failing CI with an unavailable log endpoint; the second merges. Every poll aborts before recording the second PR.

findings.title: Finish classification when GitHub definitively rejects a rerun
findings.detail: A rejected POST leaves the ledger in rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a later run_attempt that will never exist, and never emit ci.needs_fix. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-review-repro.ts"` with POST returning 422 produced `"needsFix":0,"rerunPosts":1,"pending":true` after repeated polls.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub returns 422 for the rerun request without creating another attempt. The PR remains pending indefinitely, including across restarts.

findings.title: Compare repository URL components without case sensitivity
findings.detail: GitHub repository names are case insensitive, but check_run_url is compared against the configured slug verbatim. Canonical API URL casing can therefore reject a valid job. The rerun-resolution prefix check has the same problem. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-review-repro.ts"` with configured o/r and returned O/R produced `"ledger":[],"needsFix":0,"rerunPosts":0,"pending":true` and repeated `Incomplete failing job` errors.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is configured with different capitalization from GitHub's canonical check_run_url. Every CI inspection fails before classification or rerunning.

findings.title: Existing restart-repair test fails on both base and HEAD
findings.detail: `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts -t 'verify-change: restart-repair'` exits 1 with `expect(received).toBeDefined()`, `Received: undefined`, and `0 pass / 1 fail`. The same command against a temporary snapshot of the base commit fails identically, so this is not introduced by this change.
findings.failure_scenario: Run the isolated restart-repair test; its expected resume callback remains undefined when the wait expires.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Existing escaped-process fixtures fail before exercising cleanup
findings.detail: Command: bun test test/smoke.test.ts -t 'smoke cleans CLI groups: escaped-SIGINT'. Observed: 'Expected: true; Received: false' at line 1111; 0 pass, 1 fail. The broader targeted run also failed second-SIGINT, second-SIGTERM, and escaped-timeout fixture assertions. These assertions and process-cleanup paths predate this diff.
findings.failure_scenario: The escaped child does not create its readiness marker within three seconds, so the test fails before sending the intended signal or checking cleanup.

gold.summary: Retrying an unchanged run converts inherited model chains into explicit overrides.
Routing previews remain stale after quota or cooldown expiry without an event.
Clearing a default effort omits the field from PATCH and leaves the old value stored.
Catalog history disappears on reload and does not include changes made by another client.

findings.title: Catalog history disappears when Setup is reopened
findings.detail: Catalog history comes exclusively from a component-local signal populated by this page's mutations. Navigating away or reloading erases it, and catalog changes from other clients never appear. This falls short of the requested recent catalog-change history. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probe.test.ts"` added a model through the form and remounted Setup. Output: `history before reopen= true`; after reopening, the history section contained only its heading and explanatory text. The assertion expecting the added model failed.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator adds or edits a runtime model, leaves Setup, then returns to inspect the recent change; its history is empty.

findings.title: Clearing the optional default effort silently preserves it
findings.detail: An empty effort field omits `effort` from PATCH, so RuntimeCatalog.patch merges the previous effort back in. The save succeeds while retaining the value the operator cleared. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probe.test.ts"` rendered a runtime model with effort `high`, cleared the field, and submitted through RuntimeCatalog.patch. Output: `effort before= high effort after= high`; the assertion expecting an unset effort failed.
findings.failure_scenario: A runtime model has default effort `high`; the operator empties Default effort and saves, but subsequent calls still use `high`.

gold.summary: Embedded short registered secrets remain visible in digest fields.
MCP status returns private land reasons unchanged on direct and proxy backends.

findings.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema discards run.merged, and the landed check ignores it. Reconciliation can confirm a merge without updating the saved PR snapshot or setting a resolution on a succeeded run. Probe command: `bun "$probe"`, with the script created using `mktemp "$TMPDIR/status-probe-XXXXXX.ts"`. The script created a succeeded run with an OPEN snapshot, called reconcileMergedRuns with a fake MERGED response, then passed getRunDetail through statusDetailSchema and explainStatus. Observed result: merged=true, status="succeeded", resolution=null, but state="Review needed" and nextAction="Review the current PR head; submit limitless_review with its full SHA and findings."
findings.failure_scenario: A succeeded run's PR merges externally. Merge reconciliation records merged=true while its saved PR observation remains OPEN or absent. limitless_status then requests review or landing for an already merged PR.

gold.summary: Unicode and URL encodings evade privacy protection in status and digest fields.

findings.title: Include unread PR activity when discovering review candidates
findings.detail: The digest only discovers review candidates from three event kinds. After a consumer acknowledges an approval, a subsequent head change can invalidate it and produce unread PR events without any of those kinds. Probe: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-probe.ts"` created a real temporary Store, acknowledged an approval, observed a new head, and saved a pr.ci_passed event. Observed: `unread kinds: [ "pr.ci_passed" ]`, approval `stale: true`, but digest printed `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: An approved PR's events are acknowledged, someone pushes a new head, and CI passes. The next session digest hides the PR even though its approval is stale and review is required.

findings.title: Honor the run's recorded merged flag
findings.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the merged-state check never considers it. Existing pipeline paths record confirmed merges by setting merged=true without setting a merged resolution or creating a land entry. Probe: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-probe.ts"` set merged=true on a succeeded run with an older OPEN snapshot. Observed: `run.merged: true`, but status returned `state: "Review needed"` and instructed the caller to submit limitless_review.
findings.failure_scenario: The pipeline confirms an automatic merge while the saved PR observation still says OPEN. limitless_status tells the agent to review an already merged PR.

findings.title: A throwing CI classification aborts observation of every later PR in the repository batch, every cycle
findings.detail: classifyCi throws on many conditions: non-200 REST reads, zod parse failures, and 'Incomplete …' guards. record() awaits it without a catch, so the exception leaves observe()'s loop over `known` and is only caught by tick's `.catch`. The remaining PRs in that GraphQL batch are never recorded: no state save, no merged/closed/review feed items. The failing PR keeps ciPending=true (same head), so classification runs and throws again each poll. One persistent REST problem therefore starves the whole repository's PR observation. findings.title: Signature line and feed excerpt come from the start of the log, not the failure
findings.detail: ciSignature picks the first line anywhere in the log that matches error/fail. That can be setup output, or a passing test whose name contains 'error' or 'failed' (runners such as jest --verbose, pytest -v and go test -v print passing test names). The feed excerpt is `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)` of the full log (lines 324 and 507). That is the runner preamble (runner version, OS, image, token permissions), not the failing output. The request's 'failing test or error line' and a useful needs_fix excerpt are not reliably produced. Durations embedded in the line (e.g. `[5000.01ms]`) also make the same flake produce a different signature on each run.

findings.title: Paused (main-red) PRs are fully re-inspected over REST on every poll
findings.detail: When any check is paused for main red, classifyCi returns false, so ciPending stays true and the whole inspection repeats every 15–45 s. Each repeat fetches the main commit, main check-runs, PR check-runs and statuses. For the PR's other failing checks it also re-downloads the job, annotations and full logs. With several PRs paused during a long main-red episode, this can use up a large share of the 5000/h REST budget.

findings.title: Text files that contain the literal "%PDF-" are classified as binary and reported as having NUL bytes
findings.detail: textAt sets `binary: bytes.includes(0) || bytes.includes(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))` for every blob, and binary paths are dropped from `raw`. So any edited text source that mentions "%PDF-" anywhere ends up in binaryPaths through the `!afterText.raw.has(path) && !inert.has(path)` branch. The audit then tells the author the file has "binary bytes, such as a NUL". This is why the automated audit flagged both files in this very change: both contain "%PDF-" and neither contains a NUL. It is the same wild-goose chase the request describes, from a different trigger. This predates the diff and is outside the request's scope.

findings.title: Replacing a regular file with a same-blob symlink is no longer flagged
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is also true when the mode changes but the blob ID stays the same. That includes 100644 -> 120000, a regular file replaced by a symlink with identical content. On base this was flagged, misleadingly, as binary content. With the new INERT_MEDIA_PATH guard it passes silently unless the name looks like media. New symlinks and symlinks with a changed target were never flagged on base either, so this is not a new hole. It is only an incidental check that went away without anyone deciding to remove it.

findings.title: `local` crashes on hosts that don't form a valid URL; provider matching depends on the SSH host matching the base_url origin
findings.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws a TypeError for valid SSH destinations such as a bare IPv6 address (`fe80::1`) or values with spaces, so `limitless local status` exits with a stack trace. Separately, the remote provider is found only by an exact origin match: `http://<remote_host>:8080` against `openaiBaseUrl`. If the SSH alias differs from the base_url host (an alias vs. an IP), or the provider uses `user@host` or https, nothing matches. The health probe then falls back to `http://<host>:8080/v1/models` without the API key, so it reports "unreachable", and up/down never toggle enablement. OPERATIONS.md documents the matching rule, but the failure is silent.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Line-by-line redaction of failure excerpts misses credentials that contain a newline
findings.detail: The coverage and failure-excerpt collectors receive output one line at a time, and each line is redacted on its own. If a registered credential contains a newline (for example a multi-line key), no single line contains the full value, so each piece passes through unredacted into `failures`. The `combined` tail does not have this problem because it is redacted as a whole. Today credentials come only from `src/config.ts` secrets, which are typically single-line tokens, so this is unlikely in practice.
findings.failure_scenario: A multi-line credential (such as a PEM private key) is registered, and a failing test prints it just before a `(fail)` line. The stored `failures` field then contains the key's lines unredacted, and they reach implementer feedback.

findings.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text containing the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string containing "[redacted]", whatever its source. The filter is shared by the MCP tools (mcp.ts, mcp-status.ts) and the digest CLI. Harnesses already redact credentials to "[redacted]" in agent tool results and errors, and gate output now does too. So run errors, feedback, terminal reasons and events that used to show their redacted text are now hidden entirely. So is any user prompt that contains the literal token. The request did not ask for this, it lists other command output as out of scope, and no test in the diff covers it.

With base code it returned the text unchanged. A run whose gate feedback contains a redacted credential now shows its whole feedback field as withheld

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts and strips control sequences from patches
findings.detail: `redactGateArtifact` runs `JSON.parse` and then `JSON.stringify` with no indent on every artifact that parses as JSON. It also passes the data through `redactGateData`, which adds a `confinementError` field to every object that has `ok` and `output` keys. Artifacts written with `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)` (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, review-shadow artifacts) are now served as one compact line with extra fields. Text artifacts such as diff.patch go through `stripVTControlCharacters`, so the served patch can differ from the stored one. The same VT stripping applies to the inline `patch` given to `reviewPrompt` through `redactGateData(input)`.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json used to return indented JSON and now returns a single line with `"confinementError":false` added to each result. A diff.patch that adds a fixture containing raw ESC bytes is served without them, so it no longer applies cleanly.

findings.title: Scope well beyond the request: redaction of every HTTP/SSE response and of run state
findings.detail: The request asked for one redaction point in runGates plus the deploy gate, about 30 net source lines. The change adds about 115 net source lines. It round-trips every JSON response and SSE message through `redactGateData`, which strips VT sequences, redacts all strings and injects `confinementError` into any object shaped like `{ok, output}`. It also rewrites the whole RunState on every RunContext construction (context.ts:306) and re-redacts in each prompt builder and in renderReport. Each of these runs a full JSON serialize and parse on every call, and each changes data the request did not cover. The added code is hard to tell apart from the one place that actually matters.
findings.failure_scenario: Every /api/runs, /api/feed and SSE message pays a second full JSON round trip. Any non-gate object with `ok` and `output` keys gains a `confinementError` field in API responses.
